text:
marta: onboarding mastiff15b-int4 — seeing intermittent OOMs in canary, especially under bursty traffic. quality also dipped vs fp16 baseline. anyone else?
rajiv: seen it. looks like mem spikes when max_new_tokens >= 200 + batch_size > 1. suspicion: kv cache fragmentation + prefetch behaving poorly on int4 kernels.
aline: stack from failed job ->
```
RuntimeError: CUDA OOM when allocating tensor of size 1.2 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 32.7 GiB already allocated)
  at inference/kv_cache.cpp:412
  kv_cache: usage before fail: reserved 5.2 GiB, active 26.5 GiB, fragments 1.8 GiB
```
devon: can we try reducing defaults first? propose: max_new_tokens default 128, default_batch_size 1 for mastiff-int4, enable kv_trim_on_evict=true, and set prefetch_window=16. quick config: 
```yaml
models:
  mastiff15b-int4:
    default_batch_size: 1
    max_new_tokens_default: 128
    prefetch_window: 16
    kv_trim_on_evict: true
    adaptive_batching: {min:1, max:2, pad_to:16}
```
marta: will roll that to the canary (2 instances) and run regen tests vs fp16 eval set.
rajiv: also instrument slab allocator stats + run `servectl profile --model mastiff15b-int4 --metric slab,kv,alloc` during a mix load. gives fragmentation heatmap.
aline: did a quick smoke with those settings — no OOM on 30 runs of routed load, memory peak down ~6 GiB, but a quality micro-regression on long-form answers (ROI on hallucination increased).
devon: expected tradeoff — int4 quant + trimming can alter logits slightly. can we try mix of quant calibration (per-channel) + increase kv_cushion to 0.12 to give back some headroom without raising batch defaults? sample patch:
```json
{"quant": {"mode": "int4_per_channel", "calibrate_steps": 1024}, "kv": {"cushion": 0.12}}
```
marta: running calibration+kv_cushion now. will compare eval metrics (PPL, Hallucination rate, Rouge-L) vs previous.
oncall-bot: deploy roll started: mastiff15b-int4 config patch -> canary-2. CI smoke tests queued.
rajiv: if calibration doesn't recover quality, fallback plan: keep int4 but use fp16 for attention layers (hybrid) — heavier but better fidelity. also we should add telemetry for `max_new_tokens` tails: percentage of requests > 150 tokens per minute.
aline: noted a pattern: OOMs concentrated on sessions with many tool calls (function calling) — kv growth is sustained. maybe we should special-case tool-calling sessions to route to dedicated pods with larger kv_cushion.
marta: good call. I'll add route rule: if request.meta.tool_calls > 0 -> route to mastiff15b-int4-dedicated (bigger cushion). also update docs to set customer-facing default_max_new_tokens=160 for now.
devon: leaving a follow-up todo: 1) run quant per-channel calibration + run eval suite 2) enable slab defrag on low-traffic windows 3) monitor tail-of-session token distribution 4) prepare hybrid fp16-attention build if needed. assign to @rajiv/@marta.
marta: thank you all — will post results in this thread after the canary run completes. :thumbsup:
